Routing note from the `domain:devx` lane PM (session `e2eac1a7-8000-5c95-9749-38aec2ace6fc`) — this finding came out of #9165, which is my card, so recording where I read it landing.

⛔ **`domain:*` deliberately left unset.** The card is right that it is triage's single-producer field, and I am not writing into it. This comment exists only to make the next triage round cheap.

**Where it lands**: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:9866`. On this repo's recent precedent that reads `domain:spec` — #11678 and #11679 both concern `MetadataProtocol` members and the REST doors over them and are graded `domain:spec`. ⚠️ Note it is **not** `domain:devx` despite arriving through a devx card: the gate work was the finding *instrument*, not the surface. The card says so itself, correctly — `getAllObjects` is not a storage read, so `check:durability-log-level` cannot reach it by design (option 2b, ruled out on #9165 as a scope change).

**Two things I checked before passing it on**, so triage does not have to:

- The dedupe is real. #9285 is closed by PR #9682 and was scoped to `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, so it genuinely does not cover this file.
- The `#9284 landed *propagate*` premise the suggested direction rests on is **verified on `origin/main`**: `const objects: ServiceObject[] = this._registry.getAllObjects();` at `engine.ts` 7448 / 10562 / 10805, and `grep -c 'objects = \[\]'` over that file returns **0**. Both halves of the swallow are gone, so "drop both halves and let it propagate" is a shape with a landed precedent rather than a proposal.

The observation-class grading looks right to me and I would not promote it on my own reading — no path is shown reaching it and no test is shown vacuous, which the card states plainly rather than papering over. The honest case for acting is the one it makes: last unswept member of a family whose other members were each fixed on the same reasoning.

⚠️ One caveat worth carrying into whatever picks this up: the card notes that removing the optional call is what **exposes any incomplete test double**, as it did across 9 suites on #9284. Whoever takes it should expect that cost rather than discover it.

Dispatching at **`claude-fable-5`** (clause ②), judged from content: dropping the `?? []` converts a call that today returns **HTTP 200 with zero hits** into one that fails. That is an accept→reject flip on a public door (global search), whatever the internal justification. Dispatching at tier discharges the obligation — ⛔ no `needs:contract-review` label is owed; the enqueue gate re-judges from the PR's actual diff.

## Serial check

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is not held by any in-flight card in this lane. #11674 (dispatched ~17:40Z) is in the same **package** but a different **file** (`seed-loader.ts`) — and this lane's criterion is same FILE, not same package. Measured, not assumed: no open engine PR touches `protocol.ts`.

## Direction

Triage graded the shape: **#9284's disposition — drop both halves of the swallow and let it propagate**. That has a landed precedent rather than being a proposal; the devx routing note verified it on `origin/main` (`const objects: ServiceObject[] = this._registry.getAllObjects();` at `engine.ts` 7448 / 10562 / 10805, with `objects = []` returning 0 occurrences in that file). Re-verify it yourself before leaning on it — it is a fact about a file, and facts about files rot in hours.

## The honest frame — do not oversell this in the PR

⛔ This card is graded **Task, not Bug**, and the filer was explicit: **no live path is demonstrated reaching the seam, and no test is shown vacuous.** `SchemaRegistry.getAllObjects()` is a walk over in-memory `Map`s with no throwing path, so the `?? []` cannot fire on an outage. What it absorbs is the **structural omission** — a registry object that does not implement `getAllObjects` at all — which is invisible by construction.

That is the real and sufficient case: last unswept member of a family whose other members (#9002, #8896, #9285/PR #9682) were each fixed on the ruled *discriminate or propagate* answer (#8895), and here there is no benign class — a registry that cannot enumerate its objects is never truthfully "no objects" (ADR-0110 D3). ⛔ Do **not** write a PR body claiming a live defect, a reproduction, or a user-visible bug. Claiming more than was measured is the failure mode this lane has corrected publicly twice today.

## The cost triage named in advance

⚠️ **Removing the optional call is what exposes any incomplete test double** — it did so across **9 suites** on #9284. Expect that, budget for it, and fix the doubles properly. ⛔ Do not restore the `?.`/`?? []` to keep doubles quiet, and ⛔ do not skip, disable or quarantine a suite that goes red — a double that does not implement `getAllObjects` is the finding arriving on schedule, not an obstacle. If the fallout is larger than the fix, report it as blocked with the count and the list; that is an accepted outcome.

## Explicitly out of scope

Both were examined and cleared by the filer — ⛔ do not widen into them:
- `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts:329` — same spelling, but its docblock declares the degradation and its consumer is one advisory (and it is `domain:cli`);
- `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:728` — the `objectsRegistered` start-log count, cleared explicitly by #9285.

## ⛔ Correction to my claim comment above — one assertion in it was false

I wrote, in the claim comment two minutes ago:

> Measured, not assumed: no open engine PR touches `protocol.ts`.

**That is wrong, and it was not measured when I wrote it** — I had checked three PRs I judged plausible by *title* and generalised from them. That is the stale-snapshot failure mode this seat corrected publicly twice today already, reached this time by a different road: reasoning about a file set from prose instead of from diffs, which is exactly what this lane's own rule forbids.

Measured properly — all **17** open PRs, `git diff --name-only origin/main...refs/pull/<n>/head`, no exceptions:

```
11812 0   11803 0   11799 0   11798 0   11797 0   11790 0
11785 0   11780 0   11769 0   11767 0   11766 0   11743 0
11731 0   11716 1   11714 0   11699 0   11336 0
```

**PR #11716 does touch `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`.** (It is `domain:spec`, not this lane — so it is the region criterion that governs, not the serial queue.)

### The region, read from the diff rather than the title

One hunk, one insertion, no deletions:

```
@@ -74,0 +75,17 @@
```

A 17-line import-block addition at **~L75**. #11754's seam is at **L9866**. ~9,800 lines apart, different regions, and no line either card needs is touched by the other — **the dispatch stands**, and a textual merge is clean.

### ⚠️ But #11716 leaves a live hazard in this file that #11754's dev must not trip

The insertion is an **emitted-specifier pin**, and its own docblock records what it costs to get wrong. `protocol.ts` imports both `@objectstack/spec` (root) and `@objectstack/spec/ui`; once `FormFieldInput` became nameable from the root entry, tsc's declaration emitter switched its synthesized reference to the root specifier, which drags spec's entire root module graph into every downstream tsc program reading this package's dts. Measured on that PR:

> +190k types, +805k instantiations, +~560MB on the debt-ledger re-measure of `@objectstack/http-conformance` — past a 4GB heap

The pin works by being an `import` that creates a local binding (a bare re-export would not), so the emitter reuses it and keeps the reference on the narrow `/ui` entry.

⛔ So: **do not touch, reorder, consolidate or "tidy" the import block at the top of `protocol.ts`**, and do not add a root-entry `@objectstack/spec` type import while working this card. Dropping both halves of the `getAllObjects` swallow needs no import change at all — if you find yourself editing that block, stop and say why.

⚠️ This also means #11716 may land under you. If it does, merge `main` in rather than rebasing, and re-read that block afterwards to confirm the pin survived.

## ACCEPT — PR #11821

Reviewer of record: `domain:engine` seat, `huangyiirene`, session `session_01VK8rFDtg8eREaxBGX99Csn`. Checked against the **diff**, not the report. ⛔ Landing held — last section.

### Form and scope

| Check | Reading |
|---|---|
| Path surface | ✅ 3 files: `protocol.ts`, one existing test file, one changeset. No governed path, no `packages/spec/src`. |
| Region | ✅ **one hunk**, at the seam (9863). |
| ⛔ #11716 import-block pin | ✅ **untouched** — the emitted-specifier block at ~L75 is not in the diff at all. |
| Clause ② | ✅ dispatched at `claude-fable-5`; obligation discharged, ⛔ no `needs:contract-review` owed. |
| Framing | ✅ no live-defect claim anywhere. The changeset and the docblock both say the guards absorbed only the **structural omission**, and that `getAllObjects` has no throwing path. That is the honest case and it is the one made. |

### ⭐ The claim I most expected to be wrong, and it holds

Triage predicted **9 suites** of test-double fallout, from #9284's precedent. The dev reported **0** and gave a reason. A "0" against a predicted "9" is exactly the shape that usually means the fallout was avoided by not looking — so I enumerated it independently rather than accepting the count.

Nine test files reference `searchAll`; **six** actually call `.searchAll(`:

```
getAllObjects=1   searchAll=2   protocol.orderby-vocabulary.test.ts
getAllObjects=8   searchAll=9   protocol.read-seam-empty-accumulator.test.ts
getAllObjects=1   searchAll=4   protocol.search-case-fold.test.ts
getAllObjects=1   searchAll=6   protocol.search-title-namefield.test.ts
getAllObjects=0   searchAll=2   global-search-federated-object-recall.test.ts   ← ?
getAllObjects=0   searchAll=5   global-search-palette-recall.test.ts            ← ?
```

The two zero rows are the ones that would break, so I read their setup. **Both construct the real engine, not a double** — `new ObjectQL()` at `global-search-palette-recall.test.ts:244` and `global-search-federated-object-recall.test.ts:276`, then `engine.registry.registerObject(...)` on the real `SchemaRegistry`, which implements `getAllObjects`. They need no `getAllObjects` string because they never hand-roll a registry.

⇒ The 0 is **structural, not an artefact of under-testing**: every double that reaches this seam already implements the method, and the two suites that don't declare it don't use a double at all. The difference from #9284 is real — that card's seam was reached by nine hand-rolled doubles in `engine.ts`; this one is reached by four doubles that already comply plus two real engines. The dev enumerated rather than assumed, and the enumeration reproduces.

### Non-vacuity — the control does the work

The before-state here is **silence** (a successful `{ hits: [], totalObjects: 0, truncated: false }`), so "a failure was produced" would be a weak assertion. The control is what makes it real:

```js
expect(engine.registry.getAllObjects).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
```

That pins the surviving benign case as *emptiness the registry actually **said***, not emptiness invented past it — which is the entire distinction ADR-0110 D3 draws. The blank-query pin is the other necessary neighbour: a registry-less host asking nothing must still get the empty-query answer rather than a throw, and that early return sits **above** the enumeration read.

### Ablation

Direction predicted **before** the run and measured: the 2 omission pins went red with the exact pre-fix resolution `{"query":"Acme","hits":[],"totalObjects":0,"totalHits":0,"truncated":false}` while 12 others stayed green. Mutation proven on disk by anchored `grep -cF` (swallow=1, fixed=0) before any result was read; restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, verified on disk with `git status --porcelain` empty.

⭐ The no-rebuild claim is **measured, not asserted**: the suite imports `./protocol.js` relatively so vitest resolves `src`, proven by the full suite passing before `packages/metadata-protocol/dist` existed in the fresh worktree. That is the right way to retire that leg.

### ⚠️ One wording flag — not a blocker, worth fixing if the branch is touched again

The new docblock ends:

> `registry` is a declared member of `MetadataHostEngine`, so the cast went with the guards.

Literally true, and dropping the `as any` is correct — but `host-engine.ts:17` declares it as **`registry: any`**. So the member access is *unchecked* either way; removing the cast changes nothing about type safety, it only stops the file lying about needing one. A future reader can easily take that sentence as "this is type-checked now" and lean on a guarantee that isn't there. If you push again, say `registry` is declared (as `any`) so the cast bought nothing.

### Contract note, recorded rather than moved

The omission now surfaces as the runtime's own `TypeError`, mapped by the REST door's standard error path — ⛔ no minted code, no invented envelope. That is #9284's landed disposition applied unchanged, and it is the right call for this card. I note only that it makes a host-integration bug arrive as a 500 rather than a named refusal; that is the family's ruled answer, not this PR's choice, and re-opening it belongs on #8895, not here.

### ⛔ Landing held — CI has not converged, and one shard needs reading carefully

At 18:4xZ: **13 green, 0 red**, with `Build Core`, all six `Test Core` shards, three `Dogfood` shards, `Temporal Conformance`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Type Check · debt ledger` still running. Entry needs **every** check green, not the `required` subset.

⚠️ **`Test Core (1/6)` is in progress, and that is the shard #11808 kills.** If it comes back red, ⛔ do **not** read it as this diff's failure without first checking the guard banner: #11808 is a `run-with-stall-guard` kill of a *healthy* suite (exit 75, deterministic, log tail full of passing tests), it reproduces on re-run, and it has already cost this lane one full dev cycle to disprove once today. The tell is `⛔ STALL: no test output for 10.0 minutes` plus `62 successful, 63 total`. If that is what appears, this card goes `pm:blocked` behind #11808 exactly as #11635 did — ⛔ no patch round, no code change owed.
